Get one fitted model out of an enumeration grid or a model comparison

Source: R/enumeration.R
get_candidate.Rd

get_candidate() returns one fitted model from an enumeration grid or a model comparison, for detailed inspection and further analysis. The returned object keeps its original model class and supports the summary, diagnostic, plotting and inference methods available for that model.

A candidate can be identified by its name or, for supported enumeration grids, by its class counts and model specification. When several candidates share the same class counts, the covariance structure or candidate name distinguishes them. The function retrieves the stored fit without repeating estimation.

Usage

get_candidate(x, n_profiles, n_group_classes = 1L, model = NULL)

candidate_fit(x, n_profiles, n_group_classes = 1L, model = NULL)

Arguments

x

An enumeration grid from enumerate_classes(), enumerate_lpa() or enumerate_lca() (a profile, latent class, transition or group-class family grid), or a comparison from compare_models(). On a family grid, give the name, or n_group_classes with model. A grid of mixture regressions from enumerate_regressions() is not supported (latents_bad_argument): get_results(grid, "model", n_classes = ) returns one of its models.

n_profiles

Which candidate, in one of three forms:

  • a single number: the candidate's number of profiles (classes), used together with n_group_classes and, where needed, model;

  • a name: the candidate's name as the grid's candidate column shows it, such as "profiles3_groups4";

  • two numbers: the number of profiles and the number of group classes, such as c(3, 4).

A name or a pair of numbers identifies the candidate on its own, so n_group_classes and model are then left out. For a comparison, this is the row label, as its model column shows it.

n_group_classes

Number of group classes of the candidate. Default 1, which is also the value for every candidate of a single-level grid.

model

NULL (default), or the covariance structure of the candidate as a single code such as "VVI", needed when the grid crossed several structures and the class counts match several candidates. On a group-class family grid, the family model as the grid's model column shows it, such as "additive_equal".

Value

The fitted model of the selected candidate, with the class its fitting function gives it: multilpa or multilpa_covariates from a profile or class grid, multilpa_transitions or multilpa_lta from a transition grid, multilpa_additive from a family grid. Every method and accessor of that class applies. The stored fit is returned; nothing is estimated again.

Details

A candidate is selected by its name, as the grid's candidate column shows it (get_candidate(grid, "profiles3_groups4"); classes instead of profiles when every indicator is categorical); by its class counts, get_candidate(grid, 3, 4) or get_candidate(grid, c(3, 4)); or, on a grid that crosses covariance structures, by its counts and model. From a comparison, give the row label: get_candidate(comparison, "profiles3_groups4").

candidate_fit() is the former name of get_candidate(), kept for compatibility. It takes the same arguments, forwards to get_candidate() and gives no warning.

Conditions

latents_unknown_candidate for a name or class counts not in the grid, for counts that match several candidates (the message lists their names), and for a label that is not a row of a comparison; latents_failed_candidate when the candidate's fit raised an error, so there is no model to return; latents_bad_argument for a name or pair of counts given together with n_group_classes or model, for a value that names no candidate, and for a comparison given no label; latents_incomplete_fit for a comparison that no longer carries its models. Counts that are not single positive integers, and a model that is not a single string, also raise latents_bad_argument.

Examples

# This grid crosses two structures, so the names carry them:
grid <- enumerate_lpa(faithful, c("eruptions", "waiting"),
                      n_profiles = 1:2, model = c("EEI", "VVI"),
                      n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
grid
#> Class enumeration: 4 candidate models (LPA)
#>      candidate n_profiles model log_likelihood n_parameters     aic bic_groups
#>  profiles1_EEI          1   EEI       -1516.71            4 3041.41    3055.83
#>  profiles2_EEI          2   EEI       -1157.68            7 2329.36    2354.60
#>  profiles1_VVI          1   VVI       -1516.71            4 3041.41    3055.83
#>  profiles2_VVI          2   VVI       -1147.81            9 2313.61    2346.06
#>  icl_individual profile_entropy avepp_min avepp_max avepp_mean avepp_below
#>         3055.83              NA        NA        NA         NA          NA
#>         2357.27           0.993     0.996         1      0.998           0
#>         3055.83              NA        NA        NA         NA          NA
#>         2346.52           0.999     1.000         1      1.000           0
#>  converged boundary n_best_replicated
#>       TRUE    FALSE                 2
#>       TRUE    FALSE                 2
#>       TRUE    FALSE                 2
#>       TRUE    FALSE                 2
#> Every column, unrounded: as.data.frame(x).
#> No candidate is selected automatically. Compare one convention consistently.
# By name:
get_candidate(grid, "profiles2_VVI")
#> Latent profile analysis: 2 profiles
#> 272 observations; varying diagonal residual covariance (VVI)
#> Log likelihood: -1147.806353 | AIC: 2313.613 | BIC: 2346.065
#> Converged: TRUE | iterations: 6 | best log likelihood reached by 2 of 2 starts (2 converged)
#> Smallest standardized Gaussian eigenvalue: 0.05419 (profiles, profile_2); Gaussian mass: 96.97; weight effective n: 97.02.
#> 
#> Class sizes   profile_1 64.3% (175)   profile_2 35.7% (97)
#> 
#> Means
#>  indicator profile_1 profile_2
#>  eruptions     4.291     2.038
#>    waiting    79.986    54.493
#> 
#> Variances and standard errors: get_results(x, "profiles").
#> Every other table: get_results(x, what = ), or get_results(x, "all").
# By number of profiles and structure:
get_candidate(grid, n_profiles = 2, model = "VVI")
#> Latent profile analysis: 2 profiles
#> 272 observations; varying diagonal residual covariance (VVI)
#> Log likelihood: -1147.806353 | AIC: 2313.613 | BIC: 2346.065
#> Converged: TRUE | iterations: 6 | best log likelihood reached by 2 of 2 starts (2 converged)
#> Smallest standardized Gaussian eigenvalue: 0.05419 (profiles, profile_2); Gaussian mass: 96.97; weight effective n: 97.02.
#> 
#> Class sizes   profile_1 64.3% (175)   profile_2 35.7% (97)
#> 
#> Means
#>  indicator profile_1 profile_2
#>  eruptions     4.291     2.038
#>    waiting    79.986    54.493
#> 
#> Variances and standard errors: get_results(x, "profiles").
#> Every other table: get_results(x, what = ), or get_results(x, "all").
# From a comparison, by row label:
compared <- compare_models(grid, "profiles1_VVI", "profiles2_VVI")
get_candidate(compared, "profiles2_VVI")
